rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjectival clause most naturally modifies all four preceding places of worship, since a description after coordinated phrases ordinarily returns to their shared described nouns.
rows.anchor: يذكر فيها اسم الله كثيرا } صفة والغالب في الصفة الواردة بعد جمل متعاطفة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description hints that these places are destroyed because they preserve frequent remembrance of God rather than idols; the expelled Muslims were persecuted for saying their Lord is God.
rows.anchor: وفائدة هذا الوصف الإيماء إلى أن سبب هدمها أنها يذكر فيها اسم الله كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here frequent remembrance means continuous remembrance across all times, and it signals a religious benefit of these places.
rows.anchor: في هذا إيماء إلى أن في هذه المواضع فائدة دينية وهي ذكر اسم الله

rows.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
rows.claim: Ibn Khuyz Mindad says the verse forbids demolishing the churches, synagogues, and fire temples of protected non-Muslims.
rows.anchor: قال ابن خويز منداد من أيمة المالكية ( من أهل أواخر القرن الرابع ) تضمنت هذه الآية المنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not itself forbid destroying fire temples, where God is not remembered; their protection instead follows from the dhimma covenant with Muslims.
rows.anchor: أما بيوت النار فلا تتضمن هذه الآية منع هدمها فإنها لا يذكر فيها اسم الله وإنما منع هدمها عقد الذمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative view makes the description of places where God is remembered refer only to mosques.
rows.anchor: وقيل الصفة راجعة إلى مساجد خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Monasteries come first because they were common and familiar in Arabia, serving travelers as beacons and shelter; churches follow by analogy, then prayer houses, with general mosques last.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الصوامع في الذكر على ما بعده لأن صوامع الرهبان كانت أكثر في بلاد العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise explains that God commands Muslims to defend their faith and guarantees victory: defending God’s religion is figuratively helping Him; the oath lām and emphatic nūn stress the promise, which concludes generally for the expelled Muslims.
rows.anchor: لأنهم بدفاعهم ينصرون دين الله ، فكأنهم نصروا الله ، ولذلك أكد الجملة بلام القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God being strong and mighty grounds the promised aid: strength means power, while might literally means invulnerability to anyone’s domination.
rows.anchor: العزة هنا حقيقة لأن العزة هي المنعة ، أي عدم تسلط غير صاحبها على صاحبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about those established in the land is appositional to those expelled in the preceding verse, with the intervening material parenthetical.
rows.anchor: بدل من { الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق } وما بينهما اعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, those established in the land are the emigrants, and the verse praises them and attests to the completeness of their religion.
rows.anchor: المهاجرون فهو ثناء على المهاجرين وشهادة لهم بكمال دينهم

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Uthman calls the verse praise before testing, an unseen report of what God knew about the emigrants’ future conduct.
rows.anchor: وعن عثمان : ( هذا والله ثناء قبل بلاء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their establishment means granting them the victory promised in the preceding assurance that God is capable of helping them.
rows.anchor: أي بالنصر الذي وعدناهم في قوله : { إن الله على نصرهم لقدير }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the clause is appositional to the relative phrase whoever helps God in verse 40, covering every generation of Muslims who support the religion.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بدلا من { من الموصولة في قوله : من ينصره }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either reading urges gratitude for victory by observing Islam’s foundations; that sustains victory, social cohesion, and communal stability, while abandoning them forfeits the promise.
rows.anchor: وعلى الاحتمالين فالكلام مسوق للتنبيه على الشكر على نعمة النصر بأن يأتوا بما أمر الله به من أصول الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer demonstrates commitment to religion and renews its effect within people.
rows.anchor: فأما إقامة الصلاة فلدلالتها على القيام بالدين وتجديد لمفعوله في النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving alms brings members of the community closer in their material circumstances.
rows.anchor: وأما إيتاء الزكاة فهو ليكون أفراد الأمة متقاربين في نظام معاشهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoining right and forbidding wrong lets the community itself implement Islamic rules among its members.
rows.anchor: وأما الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر فلتنفيذ قوانين الإسلام بين سائر الأمة من تلقاء أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Empowerment originally means fixing something in place and here means granting control and possession.
rows.anchor: وأصله إقرار الشيء في مكان وهو مستعمل هنا في التسليط والتمليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is generic: their rule over some portion of it applies wherever they possess land or have control.
rows.anchor: فيكون ذلك شأنهم فيما هو من ملكهم وما بسطت فيه أيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The language of empowerment recalls God’s granting people livelihoods in the earth and His enabling Joseph in the land.
rows.anchor: ولقد مكناكم في الأرض وجعلنا لكم فيها معايش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Right conduct is established religious practice, either essentials known by the whole community or detailed rulings known by scholars according to their learning.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالمعروف ما هو مقرر من شؤون الدين : إما بكونه معروفا للأمة كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the right conduct concerns fine legal details, those qualified to know them, namely scholars of differing levels, are the ones who enjoin it.
rows.anchor: وإما بكونه معروفا لطائفة منهم وهو دقائق الأحكام فيأمر به الذين من شأنهم أن يعلموه وهم العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrong is an action presented as part of Muslim religious law that religion does not accept as belonging to it.
rows.anchor: والمنكر : ما شأنه أن ينكر في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The category excludes permissible customary affairs and religious practices grounded in general principles, analogy, and legitimate juristic reasoning.
rows.anchor: فلا يدخل في ذلك ما يفعله الناس في شؤون عاداتهم مما هو في منطقة المباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse resumes the subject of the ritual appointed for every community in verse 34 after the intervening discussion of divine defense and the believers.
rows.anchor: هذا متصل في المعنى بقوله : { ولكل أمة جعلنا منسكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier communities each received one rite of approach to the one God, supporting monotheism; polytheists instead multiplied sacrificial sites, with a separate shrine for each idol.
rows.anchor: بأن الله ما جعل لأهل كل ملة سبقت إلا منسكا واحدا يتقربون فيه إلى الله لأن المتقرب إليه واحد

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha’s line uses jasad for blood poured over idols, illustrating the sacrifices made at polytheist shrines.
rows.anchor: قال النابغة : وما هريق على الأنصاب من جسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence begins anew, rather than being conjoined, because its relation to the earlier ritual statement is already clear.
rows.anchor: فالجملة استئناف . والمناسبة ظاهرة ولذلك فصلت الجملة ولم تعطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥ on both mīm and sīn, mansak is a place of ritual; here it means pilgrimage sites, whereas verse 34 means a place of sacrifice.
rows.anchor: والمنسك بفتح الميم وفتح السين : اسم مكان النسك بضمهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in nāsikūhu is accusative through omission of a preposition: they perform the rite in that place.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { ناسكوه } منصوب على نزع الخافض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muwatta reports that Quraysh stood at Qazah in Muzdalifah while other Arabs stood at Arafah, each claiming the superior station; the report says this dispute occasioned the verse and cites people of knowledge.
rows.anchor: وفي ( الموطأ ) : ( أن قريشا كانت تقف عند المشعر الحرام بالمزدلفة بقزح

rows.speaker: الباجي
rows.claim: Al-Baji, following Rabiʿa, says the verse came after pilgrimage became obligatory for Muslims but before polytheists were barred, which would date it to year nine; Ibn Ashur says the stronger view is otherwise.
rows.anchor: قال الباجي في ( المنتقى ) : ( وهو قول ربيعة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition appears addressed to the Prophet, but targets opponents: he must leave them no basis for dispute, an indirect prohibition of the listener’s causes modeled on the Arab idiom do not let me find you doing this.
rows.anchor: فالنهي ظاهره موجه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن ما أعطيه من الحجج

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes the prohibition as directed to the Messenger: because mutual-action wording can involve either party, forbidding his dispute also prevents the opponents’ counter-dispute; the result is to avoid debating them after the proofs.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : هو نهي للرسول عن منازعتهم لأن صيغة المفاعلة تقتضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The otherwise unspecified matter means monotheism, as the surrounding evidence indicates.
rows.anchor: واسم { الأمر } هنا مجمل مراد به التوحيد بالقرينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists may have claimed their Abrahamic religion was true because the Prophet affirmed pilgrimage; the verse answers that pilgrimage is a true monotheistic rite, while other rites are later falsehoods.
rows.anchor: فكان قوله تعالى : { لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا هم ناسكوه } كشفا لشبهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheist reading best fits the recurring pronouns through verse 72 and the surah’s mixed late-Meccan and early-Medinan setting; a dispute with the People of the Book is less likely.
rows.anchor: وهذا المحمل هو المناسب لتناسق الضمائر العائدة على المشركين مما تقدم إلى قوله { وعدها الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After ending the dispute, the Prophet is told to continue calling people rather than stop once proof has prevailed, since stubbornness resists persuasion and continued preaching benefits everyone; the omitted object makes the call general.
rows.anchor: عطف على انتهاء المنازعة في الدين أمر بالدوام على الدعوة وعدم الاكتفاء بظهور الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the Prophet is on straight guidance explains why he should persist in calling; it functions as a causal explanation, not as a reply to doubt.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إنك لعلى هدى مستقيم } تعليل للدوام على الدعوة وأنها قائمة مقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ʿalā is metaphorical, portraying the Prophet as firmly established upon guidance.
rows.anchor: و { على } مستعارة للتمكن من الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance is implicitly likened to a road leading to its destination; calling it straight signals swift arrival, and Islam is the easiest path to spiritual perfection.
rows.anchor: شبه الهدى بالطريق الموصل إلى المطلوب ورمز إليه بالمستقيم لأن المستقيم أسرع إيصالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This assurance strengthens the Prophet and renews his resolve to carry the burdens of the call.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا الخبر تثبيت للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم وتجديد لنشاطه في الاضطلاع بأعباء الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If decisive arguments fail to convince them and they persist in contentious mockery, the Prophet should answer that God knows what they do.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : إن تبين عدم اقتناعهم بالأدلة التي تقطع المنازعة وأبوا إلا دوام المجادلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Appealing to God’s knowledge entrusts their case to Him and indirectly ends debate, while embedding a warning suited both to their apparent demand for proof and their concealed obstinacy.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : { الله أعلم بما تعملون } تفويض أمرهم إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deeds here are their various false arguments and other forms of opposition intended to refute the truth.
rows.anchor: والمراد ب { ما تعملون } ما يعملونه من أنواع المعارضة والمجادلة بالباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The judgment sentence is an independent statement addressed to the Prophet, not part of the instructed reply to the polytheists, as the phrase between you indicates.
rows.anchor: وجملة { الله يحكم بينكم يوم القيامة } كلام مستأنف ليس من المقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s final judgment is meant to reassure and support the Messenger and the believers.
rows.anchor: والمقصود تأييد الرسول والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matter over which they differ is the same matter called al-amr in the preceding prohibition.
rows.anchor: وما كانوا فيه يختلفون : هو ما عبر عنه بالأمر في قوله { فلا ينازعنك في الأمر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage starts a new argument after the account of believers: God alone creates, human beings belong to Him, and human creation and other creatures display divine power and favor, refuting the polytheists’ central error and contrasting grateful believers with ungrateful idolaters.
rows.anchor: وهذا شروع في الاستدلال على انفراد الله تعالى بالخلق وبعظيم القدرة التي لا يشاركه فيها غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath lām and emphatic particle address polytheists as if they denied the report, because they do not act on what they know.
rows.anchor: وتأكيد الخبر بلام القسم وحرف التحقيق مراعى فيه التعريض بالمشركين المنزلين منزلة من ينكر هذا الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation means bringing into being and making, as in the cited verse about God creating what He wills.
rows.anchor: الإنشاء والصنع ، وقد تقدم في قوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes al-insān as the human species, with the definite article used generically; the pronoun in jaʿalnāhu returns to humankind.
rows.anchor: وفسر به ابن عباس ومجاهد ، فالتعريف للجنس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid likewise understands al-insān as humankind in general, rather than one individual.
rows.anchor: وفسر به ابن عباس ومجاهد ، فالتعريف للجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulāla is something drawn out from another thing, like a sword pulled from its sheath; the pattern suggests a small quantity, as in qalamāma and ṣubāba.
rows.anchor: والسلالة : الشيء المسلول ، أي المنتزع من شيء آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min marks origin: the human was formed from an extracted substance, understood as the combined reproductive material of male and female.
rows.anchor: و { من } ابتدائية ، أي خلقناه منفصلا وآتيا من سلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author describes the extract as nourishment converted into blood, male blood producing stored fatty material in the testes that becomes semen, while female blood leaves ova in the uterine channel; their union forms an embryo, ultimately from earth-derived food.
rows.anchor: وهذه السلالة هي ما يفرزه جهاز الهضم من الغذاء حين يصير دما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next stage is the union of the two extracts in the womb; the male extract is called a drop because it drips into the womb through its channel.
rows.anchor: سميت سلالة الذكر نطفة لأنها تنطف ، أي تقطر في الرحم في قناة معروفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṭfa is accusative as a circumstantial expression, while in a firm lodging is the second object of jaʿalnāhu; thumma marks elevated rank because placement there is more remarkable.
rows.anchor: منصوب على الحال وقوله : { في قرار مكين } هو المفعول الثاني

words: ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَٰهُ نُطْفَةًۭ فِى قَرَارٍۢ مَّكِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the human as derived from the extract; the sense is that God places the reproductive substance in a secure lodging, so the verse uses jaʿala with fī for placing rather than khalq.
rows.anchor: فضمير { جعلناه } عائد إلى الإنسان باعتبار أنه من السلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarār is originally the verbal noun of settling but here names the place; makīn means firmly fixed, applied to the place by a rational metaphor that emphasizes its secure condition.
rows.anchor: والقرار في الأصل : مصدر قر إذا ثبت في مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account recalls the verses describing creation from earth and then from a drop.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم قوله تعالى : { أكفرت بالذي خلقك من تراب ثم من نطفة }

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada allows al-insān to mean Adam: the sulāla is the specially selected clay from which Adam was formed.
rows.anchor: وقال بذلك قتادة فتكون السلالة الطينة الخاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Qatada’s reading, the pronoun returns to Adam as ancestor of his descendants, an instance of shifting the referent, and the sense matches the statement about Adam’s offspring.
rows.anchor: وعليه فضمير { جعلناه نطفة } على هذا الوجه عائد إلى الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks elevated rank because transforming fluid into congealed blood, with its altered density and color, is more astonishing than the initial creation of the drop.
rows.anchor: وحرف ( ثم ) في قوله : { ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة } للترتيب الرتبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name alaqa is a remarkable scientific description: anatomy shows the embryo absorbs nourishment from maternal blood through its attachment to uterine veins; alaqa means a piece of clotted blood.
rows.anchor: ومن إعجاز القرآن العلمي تسمية هذا الكائن باسم العلقة فإنه وضع بديع لهذا الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mudgha is a small piece of flesh about the size of a morsel that can be chewed.
rows.anchor: والمضغة : القطعة الصغيرة من اللحم مقدار اللقمة التي تمضغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author refers readers to the beginning of Surat al-Hajj for the stages of embryonic formation.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في أول سورة الحج كيفية تخلق الجنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa marks a near succession because clotted blood and flesh are close in nature, so their transition is proximate even though each stage lasts a long time.
rows.anchor: وعطف جعل العلقة مضغة بالفاء لأن الانتقال من العلقة إلى المضغة يشبه تعقيب شيء عن شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bones form inside the morsel, beginning the human framework of bone and flesh; this is also indicated by the following clothing of bones with flesh.
rows.anchor: وخلق المضغة عظاما هو تكوين العظام في داخل تلك المضغة وذلك ابتداء تكوين الهيكل الإنساني من عظم ولحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flesh functions like clothing for the bones; the wording does not require a period when the bones remained without flesh.
rows.anchor: فمعنى { فكسونا } أن اللحم كان كالكسوة للعظام ولا يقتضي ذلك أن العظام بقيت حينا غير مكسوة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith the author grades sound says each person is a drop for forty days, then a clot for the same period, then a morsel for the same period, after which an angel is sent to breathe in the spirit.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح : ( إن أحدكم يجمع خلقه في بطن أمه أربعين يوما نطفة ثم يكون علقة مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven stages culminate in a living being; once the spirit is breathed in, life and growth begin, a new condition distinct from the prior lifeless formation, with thumma marking rank.
rows.anchor: فإذا نفخ فيه الروح فقد تهيأ للحياة والنماء وذلك هو المشار إليه بقوله تعالى : { ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر }

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: In Umar’s council, Ali answers a claim that withdrawal is minor infanticide by saying an embryo is not infanticide until it passes through the seven stages in the verse; Umar affirms him.
rows.anchor: فقال علي : لا تكون موءودة حتى تمر عليها التارات السبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report adds that Umar was said to be the first to use the blessing may God prolong your life.
rows.anchor: فقيل : إن عمر أول من دعا بكلمة ( أطال الله بقاءك )

words: فَخَلَقْنَا ٱلْمُضْغَةَ عِظَٰمًۭا فَكَسَوْنَا ٱلْعِظَٰمَ لَحْمًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers have the plural al-ʿiẓām in both clauses; Ibn ʿAmir and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read both forms in the singular.
rows.anchor: ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم { عظما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Best of creators means best of makers, since God brings into being what no other can create.
rows.anchor: وفرع على حكاية هذا الخلق العجيب إنشاء الثناء على الله تعالى بأنه { أحسن الخالقين } أي أحسن المنشئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because human creation most immediately displays immense power, the ensuing praise first celebrates the creator’s wondrous power; baraka conveys increase.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت دلالة خلق الإنسان على عظم القدرة أسبق إلى اعتبار المعتبر كان الثناء المعقب به ثناء على بديع قدرة الخالق مشتقا من البركة

rows.speaker: الرَّضي
rows.claim: Al-Raḍi explains that tāfaʿala is originally a form of receiving an action’s effect, and when used like faʿala it conveys intensity because the state becomes firmly established.
rows.anchor: كما صرح به الرضي في ( شرح الشافية )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabāraka describes God as possessing immense goodness, namely the great good and welfare He decrees for people.
rows.anchor: فمعنى { تبارك الله } أنه موصوف بالعظمة في الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting the complements of tabāraka and khāliqīn makes the conclusion universal: God’s goodness and creation include humanity, other creatures, mountains, and heavens.
rows.anchor: وبهذا الاعتبار تكون الجملة تذييلا لأن { تبارك } لما حذف متعلقه كان عاما فيشمل عظمة الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the fire striking their faces is circumstantial to those who lost themselves; talfaḥ means to burn, with the sense of a severe impact from fire.
rows.anchor: وجملة { تلفح وجوههم النار } في موضع الحال من { الذين خسروا أنفسهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kāliḥ is someone whose lips contract and teeth show as facial nerves tighten from severe pain.
rows.anchor: والكالح : الذي به الكلوح وهو تقلص الشفتين وظهور الأسنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These rules advance the surah’s broader aim of regulating social and family dealings among neighbors, introducing visitation and permission etiquette so people follow a clear common procedure.
rows.anchor: ذكرنا أن من أكبر الأغراض في هذه السورة تشريع نظام المعاشرة والمخالطة العائلية في التجاور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission was known in pre-Islamic times and early Islam but varied by the visitor’s status and could be skipped or abbreviated; these verses standardize it as religious etiquette.
rows.anchor: وقد كان الاستئذان معروفا في الجاهلية وصدر الإسلام ، وكان يختلف شكله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A visitor may be intent on satisfying an immediate need, while an unannounced or hurried entry can embarrass or burden the host; the prescribed etiquette guards against this.
rows.anchor: وقد يتركه أو يقصر فيه من لا يهمه إلا قضاء وطره وتعجيل حاجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Homes shelter people from heat, cold, rain, and dust, and protect private matters from unwanted exposure; a resident needs time to prepare or conceal them before admitting a visitor or speaking outside.
rows.anchor: وشرع الاستئذان لمن يزور أحدا في بيته لأن الناس اتخذوا البيوت للاستتار مما يؤذي الأبدان من حر وقر ومطر وقتام

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik, as transmitted by Ibn Wahb, takes tastaʾnisū as seeking permission, glossing it as seeking welcome or familiarity with the homeowner.
rows.anchor: قال ابن وهب قال مالك : الاستئناس فيما نرى والله أعلم الاستئذان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur endorses Mālik’s interpretation as decisive: the expression is a subtle metonymy for seeking permission, in a manner that will not make the householder uneasy.
rows.anchor: وهذا كناية لطيفة عن الاستئذان ، أي أن يستأذن الداخل ، أي يطلب إذنا

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says istīnas means greeting; Ibn al-Arabi calls that remote, while Ibn Ashur explains it as greeting with the purpose of seeking permission, making the second clause explanatory.
rows.anchor: ووقع لابن القاسم في ( جامع العتيبة ) أن الاستئناس التسليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word does not mean awareness or knowing here, a separate lexical use that does not fit the context or add a useful point.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد بالاستئناس أنه مشتق من آنس بمعنى علم لأن ذلك إطلاق آخر لا يستقيم هنا فلا فائدة في ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission indicates that the host does not dislike the visitor, while refusal signals displeasure; the wording thus alludes to the reason permission is required, although only God knows the host’s heart.
rows.anchor: فإنه إذا أذن له دل إذنه على أنه لا يكره دخوله وإذا كره دخوله لا يأذن له
